proposals.premise: Production dates determine eligibility, while fit notes, restrictions and detail photos prevent misleading requests; organize the catalogue as a practical wardrobe rail with slightly mischievous tags.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows the date fields beside skirt, coat and boots; phone shows dates first, then the same pieces. Fit, restrictions and availability share each item card.
proposals.move: Enter production dates. Cards update in place: eligible pieces gain Request; unavailable ones show why, including the coat reservation on May 9–12.
proposals.tradeoff: Fast, dependable shortlisting, but visitors browse materials and construction only after committing to dates.

proposals.premise: Assume visitors have not settled feasibility: the fold-out hem, indoor-only coat and boots fitting like EU 39 may shape the production choice before dates do.
proposals.opening: Desktop opens with three large detail photographs beside concise fit and restriction notes; phone leads with one detail at a time. Hem stitching, lining and boot label share space with their consequences.
proposals.move: Choose Compare fit and restrictions. A comparison tray appears below on desktop and after the cards on phone, then accepts production dates and reveals Request or the blocking reason.
proposals.tradeoff: Supports informed decisions and exposes the May 8 after-16:00 alteration possibility, but availability takes an extra step.
